title: Powsowdie
lead:
{{Short description|Scottish sheep's-head broth or soup}}
'''Powsowdie''' is a Scottish sheep's-head [[broth]]<ref name="Davidson Jaine 2014"/><ref name="Hope 2010"/> or soup.<ref name="Newspapers.com 1971"/><ref name="dsl.ac.uk">{{cite web | title=Dictionary of the Scots Language :: SND :: Powsowdie n. | website=Dictionary of the Scots Language | url=http://dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/powsowdie | accessdate=9 September 2016}}</ref> Traditional preparation of the soup includes [[sheep's trotters]] as an ingredient.<ref name="Davidson Jaine 2014"/><ref name="Craig 1965"/> Dried peas and barley can also be used as additional ingredients.<ref name="Hope 2010"/><ref name="Duncan 2004"/> Powsowdie has been described as a speciality dish in [[Edinburgh]], Scotland.<ref name="Gillon 2016"/> Powsowdie is less popular and less known in contemporary times; it was more prominent during times when "all parts of an animal were used in cooking and nothing was wasted".<ref name="National Library of Scotland 2015"/> [[The National Library of Scotland]] included powsowdie in a 2015 food history exhibition named "Lifting the lid", which was an exhibit of historic Scottish recipe books that included example dishes.<ref name="National Library of Scotland 2015"/>
